newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations rise in latest week - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations rise in latest week - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European monetary union in 1999 rose last week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed.

Financial prices indicate that the probability assumed by the market of Italy, Spain and Sweden joining Germany and France in the first wave of EMU climbed during the week, according to the U.S. investment firm's "EMU calculator."
The probability of Italy starting EMU in 1999 rose three points to 56 percent and Spain rose six points to 74 percent. Sweden rose three points to 63 percent this week, the same as a month ago.
The calculator showed the probability of France starting EMU remains 100 percent, and expectations of Belgium's participation rose back to 100 percent from 97 percent in the previous week.
JP Morgan point out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of between three and five points.
Elsewhere, expectations of first-wave EMU participation by Portugal seven percent, while Denmark was up three percent, while the UK and Ireland dropped six and five percent respectively.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
